title: Failure of base change produces an integral normal base
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $n\ge1$ an integer
invertible on $S$ (notation of [def-kun-bc-property]). Assume
that for some $q\ge1$ the property $BC(f,n,q-1)$ holds but
$BC(f,n,q)$ does not. Then there exists a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\longleftarrow&X'&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}&&\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e}\\
S&\longleftarrow&S'&\longleftarrow&\Spec(K)
\end{array}
$$

with both squares
cartesian, where $S'$ is
affine, integral, and normal with algebraically closed function field
$K$, and an integer $d\mid n$ such that
$R^qh_*(\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z})$ is nonzero.
(*Source:* Stacks Project,
[Tag
`0F1D`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1D).) In the Stacks Project the proof uses Lemma 59.88.7,
[Tag `0F08`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F08)
(the witness diagram produced by a failure of $BC(f,n,q)$) and Lemma
59.90.2, [Tag
`0F0B`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0B) (the total direct image of $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ along
the extension of the function field is again $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$). Here $h:Y\to X'$ is the horizontal projection and $e:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the vertical projection. The function field $K=k(S')$ is as in [def-sc-function-field], $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ is the generic-point morphism, integral means [def-pc-integral-scheme], and normal means that every local ring is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. The constant cyclic sheaf is [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and its higher direct image is taken in abelian sheaves on the small etale sites, as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

proof.text: By [def-kun-bc-property], the cumulative universal condition $BC(f,n,q-1)$ gives, because $n$ is invertible on $S$, the recorded single-degree predicates $BC(f',n,r)$ for every base change $f':X'\to S'$ and every $0\le r\le q-1$. If the corresponding degree-$q$ predicate also held universally, the cumulative condition $BC(f,n,q)$ would hold: each integer $r\le q$ either satisfies $r\le q-1$ (including every negative degree, already covered by the hypothesis) or equals $q$. This contradicts the hypothesis. Thus the recorded degree-$q$ predicate fails universally, with the single-degree and universal meanings supplied by [sbc-def-base-change-property]. These are exactly the two hypotheses of the witness theorem; $n\ge1$, invertibility on $S$, and $q\ge1$ are already assumed.

Apply [sbc-lem-bc-universal-test] to obtain a base change $f':X'\to S'$ with $S'$ affine integral normal, algebraically closed function field $L$, an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/L$, and $d\mid n$ such that $R^qh_{\Omega*}\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}\ne0$, where $Y_\Omega=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $h_\Omega:Y_\Omega\to X'$. Since $n\ge1$, divisibility excludes $d=0$. Replacing $d$ by $|d|$ does not change the coefficient group: $d\mathbf Z=|d|\mathbf Z$, so the quotients and their constant sheaves agree. We henceforth take $d\ge1$, so it is also a natural-number coefficient for the invariance theorem. Set $Y_L=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}L$ and let $h_L:Y_L\to X'$ be its projection. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $Y_\Omega$ with $Y_L\times_L\Omega$ over $X'$: a map to either side is precisely a pair of maps to $X'$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with the same composite to $S'$. Write $v:Y_\Omega\to Y_L$ for the induced projection; then $h_\Omega=h_Lv$. Since $d\mid n$, write $n=da$; after pullback to the field $L$, $n$ is a unit, hence $d$ is a unit (an inverse is $a/n$). In particular $(d:L)\ne0$, the coefficient hypothesis needed for field-extension invariance.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$. For each etale $V\to X'$ define $W_V=V\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $W_{V,\Omega}=V\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and define presheaves $P_L(V)=H^q((W_V)_{\mathrm{Et}},\underline A)$ and $P_\Omega(V)=H^q((W_{V,\Omega})_{\mathrm{Et}},\underline A)$, with restrictions given by cohomological pullback. Then [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf] identifies $P_L^\#$ with $R^qh_{L*}\underline A$ and $P_\Omega^\#$ with $R^qh_{\Omega*}\underline A$. To justify precisely the cohomology groups used here, apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization] to the etale object $W_V\to Y_L$, and likewise over $Y_\Omega$. Its slice site is the small etale site of $W_V$: an etale scheme over $Y_L$ mapping to $W_V$ is etale over $W_V$ by cancellation, and conversely an etale scheme over $W_V$ is etale over $Y_L$ by composition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; the covering families are unchanged. Inverse image is restriction for these etale maps [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], and [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] identifies the restricted coefficient with the constant sheaf $\underline A$. Thus the cited sheafification theorem, which is stated using cohomology over an object, gives exactly these presheaves with their restriction maps.

source.place: Tags 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images, and 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open; applied as the local computation in Tag 0F0B(2)

proof.text: Pullback along $W_{V,\Omega}\to W_V$ gives maps $\alpha_V:P_L(V)\to P_\Omega(V)$. They commute with restrictions: for $V'\to V$ the two composites from $W_{V',\Omega}$ to $W_V$ agree, so composition and etale restriction in [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial](4),(5), together with [lem-weil-pbc-constant-pullback-composition-coherence], identify the two resulting cohomology maps. Hence $\alpha$ is a presheaf morphism. If $V$ is affine, both $V$ and $S'$ are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $V\to S'$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Its base change $W_V\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is qcqs by (3) of the same node. Apply [lem-sc-qcqs-algclosed-extension-invariance] to this morphism, the algebraically closed extension $L\subseteq\Omega$, the integer $d$ with $(d:L)\ne0$ from step 2, and degree $q$. It says precisely that $\alpha_V$ is bijective. No qcqs hypothesis on $X'$ or $Y_L$ has been used.

proof.text: For every object $V\to X'$ of the small etale site, cover $V$ by affine open subschemes $V_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Open immersions and their composites with etale maps are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2), and this jointly surjective family is a covering by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The bijections $\alpha_{V_i}$ from step 4 show local injectivity of $\alpha$ (two sections with equal images have equal restrictions to every $V_i$) and local surjectivity (lift the restriction of a target section separately through each $\alpha_{V_i}$). Thus [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] gives $\alpha^\#:P_L^\#\xrightarrow{\sim}P_\Omega^\#$. By step 3 this is an isomorphism $R^qh_{L*}\underline A\cong R^qh_{\Omega*}\underline A$. Its right side is nonzero by step 2, so its left side is nonzero as well: otherwise the isomorphism would identify the right side with zero. Retain $S',X',d$ and the first Cartesian square from step 2, take $K=L$, $Y=Y_L$, and $h=h_L$. The second square is Cartesian by the construction of $Y_L$. All the required clauses now hold, with $K$ the function field itself.

tool_uses.why: This is exactly the constant-cyclic cohomology clause of the explicitly named 0F0B input, applied only to the qcqs schemes W_V; the present unit has no field-extension invariance node.

Generic coefficient comparison coherence is needed when replacing inverse images of constant sheaves by constant sheaves in the presheaf naturality square.
Generic identification of etale inverse image with restriction, needed for the coefficients in the local higher-image computation.
Generic abelian etale higher-direct-image computation by sheafified object cohomology, used to implement the local 0F0B comparison; no such computation is stated in this unit.
